task_instance: Write a repo-backed engineering design doc for adding per-client rate limiting to a small HTTP quote API, following the skill's default section shape, design discipline, and contract-matrix completeness gate.
evidence: Read the skill (SKILL.md) and its referenced references/review-prompts.md from the skill repo. Created a minimal realistic sample repo at sample_api/app/server.py (a tiny http.server app whose ROUTES dict is the source of truth for path->handler) so the design could be repo-backed and inspect real owners. Produced the deliverable design-rate-limit.md (1143 words) using the skill's default shape. Verified with a python3 check: all 8 required sections present (Summary, Problem Statement, Goals, Non-Goals, Current State, Proposed Design, API / Contract Changes, Detailed Behavior); zero forbidden implementation-planning artifacts (no checkboxes, no milestones, no owner assignments, no commit/push steps); contract matrix present (Supported/Rejected/Default/Source Of Truth/Placement/Routing/Naming/Equivalence/Proof columns filled); a one-request decision table present; proof obligations stated as properties to prove (e.g. N+1 requests in one window yield exactly N handler calls and one 429 with Retry-After in (0,W]) rather than file edits or command sequences; optional sections (Alternatives Considered, Risks And Tradeoffs, Open Questions) used only where they aid review. No model calls, external services, credentials, or MCP/connector tools were used.
